source: Si, Hashimoto, Yang (2025) The Ideation-Execution Gap, Appendix D
finding: Ideation scores barely predict execution scores. Gap 2 answered: the correlations are weak, and for AI ideas the excitement correlation is moderately negative.
numbers: Pearson r between ideation and execution score, AI ideas: novelty -0.019, excitement -0.321, effectiveness 0.172, overall -0.092. Human ideas: novelty -0.084, excitement 0.205, effectiveness 0.022, overall 0.158. Spearman for human ideas: -0.148, 0.183, -0.092, 0.124. The Spearman row for AI ideas is garbled in the PDF text (values seen: 0.077, -0.386, 0.110, -0.092).
quote: the correlation is weak in most cases, and for AI ideas, there is even a moderately negative correlation
limits: No confidence intervals in the table. About 20 ideas per arm, so each r has a very wide interval. Column order for the Spearman rows assumed to match the Pearson rows.
agent_relevance: A model's pre-run score of its own ideas is close to useless as a pursuit signal. Do not rank ideas by a pre-run score alone; require a cheap executed probe.

source: Si et al. (2025) Ideation-Execution Gap, Appendix G (metric correlations)
finding: After execution, the overall score is driven by novelty and excitement more than by effectiveness. Changes in overall score track changes in novelty and excitement.
numbers: Table 11 (execution scores): overall vs novelty 0.616, excitement 0.771, soundness 0.635, effectiveness 0.654; novelty vs effectiveness only 0.291. Table 12 (score changes ideation to execution): overall change vs novelty change 0.809, vs excitement change 0.856, vs effectiveness change 0.642.
limits: Same N=43 NLP study. Correlations among reviewer scores, not against any outside ground truth.
agent_relevance: Novelty and working-ness are weakly linked (r 0.29). A novelty-first pursuit rule can pick ideas that do not work.

source: Mule, Garikaparthi, Patwardhan (2026) Teaching Language Models to Forecast Research Success Through Comparative Idea Evaluation
finding: Gap 4 partly answered. On 11,488 idea pairs from PapersWithCode leaderboards, an off-the-shelf 8B model is below chance, GPT-5 zero-shot is above chance but far from reliable, and a small fine-tuned model beats GPT-5.
numbers: Off-the-shelf 8B: about 30% (Llama 3.1 30.03%, Qwen3 20.14%). GPT-5 zero-shot 57.65%; with low/medium reasoning 59.61%/61.10%. SFT 8B: 77.10%. RLVR about 71.35%. 724 benchmarks. Accuracy is consistency-aware (a pair counts only if right under both orderings), so 50% is not the floor.
limits: Pairs come from published papers, so leakage and survivorship bias are possible. SFT gain is on the same-distribution test. Table text is partly garbled; abstract numbers used. Gemini 2.5 Flash 40.73%.
agent_relevance: Frontier models beat chance on pairwise outcome prediction in 2026 but only by about 10 points. Training on outcomes adds more than a stronger model. Outcome priors beat prompting.

source: Mule et al. (2026) cross-domain and independent test sets
finding: On Wen et al.'s independently built test set, a fine-tuned 8B model beats Wen's zero-shot GPT-4.1 with retrieval. On a cross-domain time-split, all models fall.
numbers: Wen test set: Reason-SFT-DrGRPO 67.49% vs GPT-4.1 + retrieval 51.4% (figure taken from Wen et al.). Cross-domain (CD) test: GPT-5 42.84% to 45.96% by reasoning effort; best trained models about 45 to 49%. Base Qwen3 3.55% to 12.62% on CD.
limits: The 51.4% is copied from Wen, not re-run. Metric definitions differ between papers (consistency-aware vs plain).
agent_relevance: Outcome prediction does not transfer across domains. Any forecasting prior must match the domain, or the agent should fall back to running a probe.

source: Mule et al. (2026) role of reasoning
finding: More thinking helps GPT-5 only a little, and naive chain-of-thought prompting can hurt a small model on idea-outcome forecasting.
numbers: GPT-5 accuracy 57.65% (none), 59.61% (low), 61.10% (medium), gains diminishing. Llama 3.1 8B with a CoT instruction: 30.02% down to 27.38%. Qwen3 thinking variant about +5 points. Synthetic-reasoning SFT 25.54% vs reason SFT 37.51%; RL then recovered about 71%. Reward hacking seen (model stopped writing reasoning).
limits: One benchmark family; consistency-aware accuracy.
agent_relevance: Do not assume a longer deliberation step improves the S0 appraisal; measure it against outcomes.

source: Zuo, Zhu (2025) Strategic Scaling of Test-Time Compute: A Bandit Learning Approach
finding: Gap 6 answered for the query-allocation case: elimination and bandit allocation beat uniform allocation of a fixed sample budget when a reward oracle scores candidates.
numbers: Up to +11.10% absolute (15.04% relative) on MATH-500, +10.82% (14.44%) on AIME25, +11.23% (15.29%) on LiveCodeBench vs uniform. At average budget 8: Llama-3.1-8B +7.41 points (3.11x efficiency); DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B +9.97 points (4.00x). Streaming and token-matched variants also beat uniform.
limits: Arms are queries with verifiable answers, not research ideas. The reward oracle is a PRM or LLM judge assumed fairly accurate. Gains shrink for strong models.
agent_relevance: Equal-budget adaptive allocation works when the score is informative. For ideas the scorer is not informative (d01), so the gain may vanish.

source: Zuo, Zhu (2025) frontier-model and hard-subset results
finding: With a strong reasoning model the gain is small. On hard queries an entropy rule learns to spend on solvable queries and not on unsolvable ones.
numbers: Gemini-2.5-Flash-Lite with Gemini-3.0-Flash as judge: +3.4 points accuracy (3.66% relative), over 2x efficiency; coverage +2.4 points. MATH-500-Hard-16 (56 queries): the entropy extension sends more compute to solvable queries. Unsolvable ones give invalid or low-entropy outputs.
limits: Entropy proxy tied to math answer format. No head-to-head of UCB vs successive halving vs Elo on ideas.
agent_relevance: Spend on candidates whose samples stay varied and well formed; stop on candidates whose probes collapse. Gap 6 stays open for idea-level arms.

source: Zhang (2026) Budgeted Subset Refinement for Execution-Aware LLM Research Ideation
finding: Gaps 1 and 6 at proxy level: refining only a chosen subset of ideas beats refining all uniformly on cost per strong idea. Random-k is a strong cheap baseline. Diversity-aware MMR-k is best.
numbers: 10 seeds x 10 ideation environments. Strong non-duplicate yield: MMR-k 23.70, random-k 22.18; MMR minus fixed refine-all +1.90, CI [0.20, 3.60]. Cost per strong idea: MMR 4492 vs random 4859 tokens; MMR minus fixed -895 [-1327,-498], 9/10 seeds. Duplicate rate 0.172 (MMR) vs 0.186 (random); MMR beats fixed on duplicates in 10/10 seeds. Raw generation plus reranking gave zero strong non-duplicate ideas.
limits: Single independent author; rubric and LLM judges, no execution. A blinded external-judge check on 72 items supports refinement but per-item rankings of strategies vary by judge. MMR vs random yield difference +1.52, CI [-0.22, 2.82], not significant.
agent_relevance: At equal tokens, a random or diversity-based subset for deeper work is hard to beat on a proxy. A score-ranked pick is not shown better. Still untested against executed outcomes.

source: Zhang (2026) Budgeted Subset Refinement: limits and paired tests
finding: The paper states its claims are proxy-only and that rankings among refined strategies depend on the judge.
numbers: Seed-paired tests: MMR vs random cost per strong -367 tokens, 9/10 seeds; random vs fixed -528 [-1325,-45], 7/10. Micro-low triage vs fixed: -205 with a garbled interval.
quote: do not substitute for expert review or execution-grounded validation
limits: No execution ground truth. The judge LLMs are the same class that fails at idea judging in Si 2024.
agent_relevance: Supports a diversity-aware pursuit selector as a cheap default; does not show it improves real outcomes.

source: Shahid et al. (2025) Literature-Grounded Novelty Assessment of Scientific Ideas
finding: Gap 8 answered: a retrieve-then-rerank checker with expert-labelled examples reaches 0.81 accuracy on a small expert known-versus-novel set. Other checkers are far lower.
numbers: Test set 32 ideas (35 train). Idea Novelty Checker (gpt-4o, 15 expert examples, with idea, papers, class, reasoning): accuracy 0.81, F1 0.79, kappa 0.59. Zero-shot 0.68. TextGrad prompt 0.78. OpenReview examples 0.75 (0.59 without papers). AI Scientist novelty prompt 0.47, kappa 0.05 (defaults to not novel 18 of 32 times). AI Researcher prompt 0.78 (GPT-4o), 0.56 (Claude 3.5 Sonnet).
limits: Tiny test set (32). Retrieval fixed to the expert's top-10 papers in the prompt comparison. gpt-4o in 2024; no 2026 reasoning models. Kappa 0.59 is moderate agreement.
agent_relevance: A novelty gate that reads retrieved papers works much better than keyword checks, but the sample is too small to trust the exact numbers.

source: Shahid et al. (2025) ablation of retrieval and reranking
finding: What makes the checker work is facet-based reranking of retrieved papers, not the LLM verdict alone.
numbers: Accuracy on 'not novel' cases (58 ideas: 13 not-novel from the test set plus 45 NLP papers, o3-mini judge): complete system 89.66%; relevance RankGPT 13.79%; embedding filter only 10.34%; snippet retrieval 8.62%; keyword retrieval 5.17%. About 30% of top-10 papers differ across rerankers.
limits: Measures recall of 'not novel' on 13 cases plus papers known to exist. Small.
agent_relevance: Retrieval quality is the bottleneck of the novelty check. Spend S0 budget on retrieval and reranking, not on longer verdict reasoning.

source: Relative Neighbor Density paper (2025) Enabling AI Scientists to Recognize Innovation
finding: A non-LLM density method beats LLM novelty judges across domains in AUROC, but its labels come from a recency-and-citation proxy, not experts.
numbers: AUROC: RND 0.820 (NeurIPS), 0.765 (Nature Medicine), 0.795 (mixed). Sonnet-3.7 with literature search: 0.813, 0.616, 0.597. Historical dissimilarity 0.856, 0.699, 0.362. Overall-novelty 0.584, 0.544, 0.456.
limits: Positives are recent top-venue papers, negatives are old highly cited papers. That labels age and fame, not true novelty. Several arXiv versions exist.
agent_relevance: Treat as a cheap reference-density feature, not a truth source.

source: Relative Neighbor Density paper (2025) LLM judges without search
finding: Without a search tool, reasoning-model novelty judgment is near random. With search it holds in CS but drops in other fields.
numbers: No search: AUROC about 0.5. With search, Sonnet-3.7: about 0.8 on NeurIPS, about 0.6 on Nature Medicine and mixed. Authors say mixed-domain RND about 0.78 vs others 0.6 or below.
limits: Same proxy-label caveat. Single group.
agent_relevance: The S0 novelty gate must retrieve, and should be expected to degrade outside the model's home field.

source: LiveIdeaBench (2024-2025) arXiv 2412.17596
finding: Gap 10 stays open, with context added: scientific-idea quality is only weakly tied to general reasoning scores, but all scoring is by an LLM judge panel, not execution.
numbers: 41 models, 1,180 keywords, 22 domains. Correlation of idea score with general intelligence score r=0.357 (p=0.038, 95% CI 0.022 to 0.621, r2=0.127). Idea length vs quality r=0.089 (n about 286,490, r2=0.008). QwQ-32B-preview ranked 8 of 41, near Claude 3.7 Sonnet thinking.
limits: Dynamic panel of top-10 LLMs as judges (max 20% per organisation, self excluded). Authors admit the panel limits measurement of originality and feasibility. No executed ideas.
agent_relevance: Do not choose the idea-generating model by its reasoning benchmark, and do not read the judge panel as outcome evidence.

source: Yamada et al. (2025) The AI Scientist-v2
finding: Gap 9: v2 uses four staged experiment phases with stop criteria (a cheap stage-1 prototype gate), but no ablation tests whether the gate saves budget.
numbers: Stages: 1 preliminary investigation (ends when a basic prototype runs), 2 hyperparameter tuning, 3 research agenda, 4 ablations. 3 manuscripts submitted to an ICLR workshop among 43 submissions; one accepted with scores 6, 6, 7 (mean 6.33), two rejected. Authors' own review: none met main-track quality.
limits: N=3 papers. No comparison with a single-gate or no-gate variant. Workshop acceptance is not a quality measure.
agent_relevance: A stage-1 probe is standard in agent systems but unproven as a budget saver. Gap 9 stays open.

source: Regan, Gournail, Oka (2024) Problem-Solving in Language Model Networks
finding: Gap 7 partly answered, and a Zollman direction is not reproduced: isolated agents did worst, connected ones better, and random sparse networks matched fully connected ones.
numbers: GPT-3.5-Turbo agents, 100 MATH questions, each run 3 times, 4 debate rounds, majority vote. Accuracy: fully connected 67.7 +/- 1.1% (125,000 tokens per round); fully disconnected 63.9 +/- 0.4% (5,000); random 68.2 +/- 0.5% (28,600); scale-free 64.8 +/- 1.0% (21,800). Disconnected accuracy fell after round 2.
limits: Weak model, one dataset, 100 questions. Agents see each other's answers from round 1, so the early-isolation condition of Zollman is not tested. Differences are about 4 points.
agent_relevance: Sharing late and sparsely is cheap. Isolate-then-share (diversity first) remains untested, so keep the schema's independent-sample step as a hypothesis only.

source: Lin et al. (2026) DN-Hypo-Pipeline
finding: Gap 5 partly answered: the only controlled test found of a philosophy-of-science explanation scaffold (Hempel DN, Salmon, Armstrong) versus direct prompting. It wins, but compute is not matched, and it is not Darden or Nickles.
numbers: 3 explananda (ResNet, Transformer, word embedding). 5 law-guided proposals vs 1 direct baseline each. 4 judge LLMs plus 3 PhD experts, 7 raters. Wilcoxon signed-rank: max and mean score significant for both groups; median test p=0.0859 for LLMs (not significant), significant for humans. Idea-only judging ablation also favours law-guided. Two top ideas were implemented: lower Transformer complexity; competitive embeddings with fewer parameters.
limits: Five proposals versus one baseline is best-of-5 versus a single sample, a compute and selection confound. Tiny N, proof of concept, no token counts.
agent_relevance: Weak positive for explanation-structure scaffolds, but a best-of-N control is missing. Run an own test at equal tokens.

source: Shi et al. (2026) EarlyEval: Cheaper Agent Evaluation via Early Outcome Prediction
finding: Analogue to gap 1 (not ideas): a lightweight classifier on partial agent trajectories predicts outcome early and cuts cost with almost no change in resolve rate.
numbers: SWE-bench Verified, TerminalBench, Toolathlon: 13% to 26% fewer steps, up to 44.1% fewer input tokens and 29.4% fewer output tokens at 89% to 97% prediction accuracy. At threshold 0.95, SWE-bench steps -26.0%, resolve-rate shift 1.1 points; Toolathlon -23.0% at 0.90, 0.9 points.
limits: Pass/fail tasks with reference solutions; features include reference-solution similarity, which research ideas lack. Not research ideas.
agent_relevance: Partial runs are informative for pass/fail tasks. A mid-run probe check for pursuit is plausible; for ideas no test exists.

source: Si, Hashimoto, Yang (2026) ICLR 2026 poster record of the Ideation-Execution Gap
finding: Gap 3 stays open: web searches for a replication outside NLP, with 2026 reasoning models or larger N, found only the original study, accepted at ICLR 2026.
numbers: Search results only (snippet level). Original N=43 executors, one field.
limits: Absence of evidence from a limited search, not a systematic review. Page not opened.
agent_relevance: Treat the gap as an unreplicated single study when weighting it.

source: Cross-check of Si et al. (2025) gaps against Mule et al. (2026) forecasting
finding: Si's blind-proposal appraisal and Mule's trained forecaster are different tasks. The first fails (see d01); the second reaches 71 to 77% only on paper pairs from the same distribution.
numbers: Si execution-vs-ideation gaps: AI ideas -1.049 (novelty), -1.760 (excitement), -1.879 (effectiveness), -1.976 (overall) vs human -0.010, +0.078, -0.052, -0.628 (values re-checked in the critique). Mule: GPT-5 61.1% vs fine-tuned 8B 77.1%.
limits: Cross-study comparison of different tasks; a judgment, not a measured result.
agent_relevance: Outcome-trained forecasters are the only appraisal that clearly beats chance. Use them as one signal next to a cheap probe.
